must_find.summary: SQL injection: the `sort` query parameter is interpolated into ORDER BY via f-string without an allowlist.
Missing authorization: any logged-in user can list any other user's orders (no can_access_user check / 403), violating requirement 1 (IDOR).
Requirement 2 not met: no 404 when the user does not exist (returns an empty list instead).
N+1 queries: one order_items query per order inside the loop; should batch with ANY/IN or a join.
CREATE INDEX without CONCURRENTLY on a ~40M-row live table blocks writes for the duration of the build.

nice_to_find.summary: Index (user_id) does not support ORDER BY created_at / total; should be composite e.g. (user_id, created_at DESC); order_items.order_id also has no index.
Cursor uses `id < after` while sorting by created_at or total, so pages skip or repeat rows; keyset cursor must match the sort key.
int(limit) on non-numeric input raises and returns 500 instead of 400; negative limit not rejected.

must_not_flag.summary: The user_id / after / limit values are passed as %s parameters; these are NOT SQL injection.

Reading SECRET_KEY from an environment variable must NOT be called a security issue (hardcoded secret, secret exposure, insecure config). Noting it as out-of-scope or a startup KeyError is fine and does NOT count as flagged.
Lack of rate limiting / DoS concerns (explicitly excluded).
